# PullQuote

A quotation set apart from the text with a gold rule, in the reading typeface and italic.

```tsx
import { PullQuote } from '@kafka-ds/react'
```

## When to use it

- To lift one memorable line out of a long text, or to quote a source at length.
- At most one or two per article; they are a pause, not a rhythm.

## When not to

- As a replacement for the original sentence: if it is only in the pull quote, a reader who skips it misses it. Repeat, do not move.
- For testimonials with a photo and a name: use a card.
- Gold text. The rule is gold (3:1 border gold); the words stay ink.

## Examples

### With attribution

Use it for a line you want the reader to remember, taken from the text itself or from a source.

```tsx
<PullQuote attribution="Cuaderno de clase, 2026">Escribir es decidir qué no se dice.</PullQuote>
```

### Without attribution

A line taken from the same text needs no attribution.

```tsx
<PullQuote>La puntuación es la respiración del texto.</PullQuote>
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `children` (required) | `ReactNode` |  | The quoted text. |
| `attribution` | `ReactNode` |  | Who said it: a name, or a name and a work. Rendered in a `figcaption`. |
| `cite` | `string` |  | URL of the source, exposed as the `cite` attribute of the block quote. |
| …rest | `HTMLAttributes<HTMLElement>` | | Everything else is passed to the underlying element. |

## Accessibility

- **Semantics:** `figure` with a `blockquote`, and a `figcaption` for the attribution. `cite` carries the source URL.
- **Contrast:** quote and attribution are 7:1; the rule is 3:1 against the page (non-text contrast).
- Screen readers announce it as a figure with a caption; the dash before the author is decorative text and reads as a pause.

## Content

- Keep it under about 20 words.
- Attribute with a name and, if useful, a work: "Cuaderno de clase, 2026".
